beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route carries the claim and the panes to the new name, and keeps what agents said they were doing with the board.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality route keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check
nodes.description: The render route reads an optional against: the variant a picture is drawn relative to. It refuses a variant the board lacks, and the drawn variant itself, as an unknown variant.

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write, and moves what the server keyed by the old name: its panes, its claim, what the agent said
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, answers its tracked embeds or the nodes that open it, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). A BOARD_OPENED_BY refusal carries openedBy. The pane hears board_note with discarded, reads the board again and finds it missing, as after a move; the browser offers no delete.

nodes.name: Service routes
nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, the health answer (the archboard-server service, its pid, the checkout whose source it runs and whether that is the source on disk) and the vault a page opens in
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid. A CLI refuses a server whose health names another checkout's source than its own, and names both checkouts. The vault a page opens in is the one call that names no vault.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling over a period on request as checkout work; keeps each answer in memory until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: reads the board and the proposal named, then asks the history lens for the parts a branch changed; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, which needs no vault: the loopback refusal, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant of each vault, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and onto bound declarations for locality and footprint; labels path-wide fallback when a symbol cannot be resolved

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, container interfaces and document references to the code they name, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call that names no vault, a vault the server cannot read, or a directory that is not the .archboard/vault of one, before any handler runs
nodes.description: ADR 0049: every call names its vault as ?vault=<directory> or a vault field in its body. The refusal says how to name one (VAULT_REQUIRED, 400; VAULT_UNREADABLE, 404) and creates nothing. TASK-472.09: a vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault is VAULT_UNREADABLE too, and the refusal says to move the boards there, because a workhorse works in the directory that holds the vault (ADR 0050) and such a vault has none. A handler reads the canonical vault with vaultOfRequest.

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which repository identity the vault's own checkout holds, and which checkout holds any other
nodes.description: The board listing needs it: a drill-down that names the vault's own repository is a link within the vault, not a link out of it (ADR 0049).

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it
nodes.description: GET /api/repositories answers under the settings-read browser-origin guard; PUT /api/repositories/chosen {repository, root} answers under the mutation guard, as the opener settings do. Neither names a vault, because the list and the choice belong to the machine. A root that is not a known checkout of the repository is refused (CHECKOUT_UNKNOWN, 404): the page offers nothing else, and the route never registers one. The server watches the registry file from start to stop and follows every change it has not followed yet: the menu's choice, an agent's show or a finished move that chose, a repo command or the first command in a checkout, and another server's show. Then every pane in the vault of a checkout that is not chosen moves to the chosen one, keeping its board, every other pane hears the name its repository goes by now, and every tab hears repositories_changed.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route carries the claim and the panes to the new name, and keeps what agents said they were doing with the board.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality route keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

nodes.name: Locality route

nodes.name: Footprint route

nodes.name: Live panes

nodes.name: Application lifetime

nodes.name: Codex workbench

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and onto bound declarations for locality and footprint; labels path-wide fallback when a symbol cannot be resolved

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, container interfaces and document references to the code they name, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call that names no vault, a vault the server cannot read, or a directory that is not the .archboard/vault of one, before any handler runs
nodes.description: ADR 0049: every call names its vault as ?vault=<directory> or a vault field in its body. The refusal says how to name one (VAULT_REQUIRED, 400; VAULT_UNREADABLE, 404) and creates nothing. TASK-472.09: a vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault is VAULT_UNREADABLE too, and the refusal says to move the boards there, because a workhorse works in the directory that holds the vault (ADR 0050) and such a vault has none. A handler reads the canonical vault with vaultOfRequest.

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which repository identity the vault's own checkout holds, and which checkout holds any other
nodes.description: The board listing needs it: a drill-down that names the vault's own repository is a link within the vault, not a link out of it (ADR 0049).

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it
nodes.description: GET /api/repositories answers under the settings-read browser-origin guard; PUT /api/repositories/chosen {repository, root} answers under the mutation guard, as the opener settings do. Neither names a vault, because the list and the choice belong to the machine. A root that is not a known checkout of the repository is refused (CHECKOUT_UNKNOWN, 404): the page offers nothing else, and the route never registers one. The server watches the registry file from start to stop and follows every change it has not followed yet: the menu's choice, an agent's show or a finished move that chose, a repo command or the first command in a checkout, and another server's show. Then every pane in the vault of a checkout that is not chosen moves to the chosen one, keeping its board, every other pane hears the name its repository goes by now, and every tab hears repositories_changed.

nodes.name: Repository listing
nodes.responsibility: Turns the checkout registry into the repositories the navigator lists: each identity's chosen checkout, its vault and its state, and the names of the vaults
nodes.description: An identity is listed when any known checkout has a vault in the .archboard/vault layout; its state is ready, no-vault, gone or unchosen. The registry is the only source: no environment variable names a vault (TASK-472.09). A vault whose link leads out of the layout is no vault here, because every call to it is refused: its checkout reads no-vault, and an untracked one is not listed. The vault a page opens in is that of the first ready repository by name, else none. repositoryOfVault is how a show names the repository a pane moved into. A vault that no registry entry holds has no repository name, and its checkout is the directory that holds it.

nodes.name: Checkout registry
nodes.responsibility: Which checkouts of each repository this machine knows, which one is chosen, and the untracked vaults

nodes.name: Move route
nodes.responsibility: Moves a whole board into another repository's vault under the write's admission, tells each vault's panes and takes the board's panes along; says beforehand what a move would rewrite
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051: semantic move. move.to names the target vault, read as strictly as the vault of the call. The source vault's change feed says the board moved and where to. A move that stopped part way announces what it wrote, moves no pane, and answers MOVE_STOPPED. TASK-472.16: movePreviewRoute answers GET move-preview, holding and writing nothing, so it takes no lease and no claim; it can be out of date when the move runs, and the version it answers is the version the move states. A board name that cannot be used is refused as every write refuses it (BAD_BOARD_NAME, through usableBoard), and any other refusal is answered in the move's own words and codes.

nodes.name: Board writes
nodes.responsibility: The routes that change a board or its claim: the write boundary, claim, rename, embed tracking, discard and move. Each runs as tracked mutation work, and each change is announced to the panes.

nodes.name: Reads and server health
nodes.responsibility: Routes reads, server health and checkpoint retention without changing current architecture

nodes.name: Code checks on request

nodes.name: Repositories and checkouts

nodes.name: Historical correction routes

nodes.name: Track embed route

nodes.description: ADR 0057. semantic render and rasterize --track call it before they write the file.

nodes.name: Canonical model routes

nodes.description: Every request names its vault. The shared runtime owns retention, dependency and evidence semantics. Browser selection opens an exact checkpoint through the same read contract.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route carries the claim and the panes to the new name, and keeps what agents said they were doing with the board.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality route keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check
nodes.description: The render route reads an optional against: the variant a picture is drawn relative to. It refuses a variant the board lacks, and the drawn variant itself, as an unknown variant.

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write through the store, which moves its claim and what the agent said; points the server's panes at the new name
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, answers its tracked embeds or the nodes that open it, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). A BOARD_OPENED_BY refusal carries openedBy. The pane hears board_note with discarded, reads the board again and finds it missing, as after a move; the browser offers no delete.

nodes.name: Service routes
nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, the health answer (the archboard-server service, its pid, the checkout whose source it runs and whether that is the source on disk) and the vault a page opens in
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid. A CLI refuses a server whose health names another checkout's source than its own, and names both checkouts. The vault a page opens in is the one call that names no vault.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check, through the one code check the server keeps

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling on request as checkout work: names the board and variant to the history lens, which picks the variant and keeps each answer

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: names the board and proposal to the history lens, which reads them and chooses the variants; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, which needs no vault: the loopback refusal, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory

nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and bound declarations for locality and footprint; reads the board a request names and chooses the variants it reads; labels path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, interfaces and document references to the code they name, at the current variant or the named draft; one run gives behind beside it
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route asks the store to rename the board. The store carries the claim and what agents said they were doing to the new name, and the route points every pane on the board at the name it has now.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality reading keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none. The history lens reads the board a locality or footprint request names, so the route sends names and maps the refusal to a status.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

beats.heading: A correction reads the code with no lease held
beats.body: A historical correction must be checked against the code at the revisions it cites. The store prepares the candidate first and holds nothing, the route reads Git, and the commit then writes exactly that candidate, refusing it when the board moved while Git was read.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check
nodes.description: The render route reads an optional against: the variant a picture is drawn relative to. It refuses a variant the board lacks, and the drawn variant itself, as an unknown variant.

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write through the store, which moves its claim and what the agent said; points the server's panes at the new name
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, answers its tracked embeds or the nodes that open it, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). A BOARD_OPENED_BY refusal carries openedBy. The pane hears board_note with discarded, reads the board again and finds it missing, as after a move; the browser offers no delete.

nodes.name: Service routes
nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, the health answer (the archboard-server service, its pid, the checkout whose source it runs and whether that is the source on disk) and the vault a page opens in
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid. A CLI refuses a server whose health names another checkout's source than its own, and names both checkouts. The vault a page opens in is the one call that names no vault.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check, through the one code check the server keeps

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling on request as checkout work: names the board and variant to the history lens, which picks the variant and keeps each answer

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: names the board and proposal to the history lens, which reads them and chooses the variants; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, which needs no vault: the loopback refusal, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant of each vault, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and bound declarations for locality and footprint; reads the board a request names and chooses the variants it reads; labels path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, interfaces and document references to the code they name, at the current variant or the named draft; one run gives behind beside it
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call that names no vault, a vault the server cannot read, or a directory that is not the .archboard/vault of one, before any handler runs
nodes.description: ADR 0049: every call names its vault as ?vault=<directory> or a vault field in its body. The refusal says how to name one (VAULT_REQUIRED, 400; VAULT_UNREADABLE, 404) and creates nothing. TASK-472.09: a vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault is VAULT_UNREADABLE too, and the refusal says to move the boards there, because a workhorse works in the directory that holds the vault (ADR 0050) and such a vault has none. A handler reads the canonical vault with vaultOfRequest.

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which repository identity the vault's own checkout holds, and which checkout holds any other
nodes.description: The board listing needs it: a drill-down that names the vault's own repository is a link within the vault, not a link out of it (ADR 0049).

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it
nodes.description: GET /api/repositories answers under the settings-read browser-origin guard; PUT /api/repositories/chosen {repository, root} answers under the mutation guard, as the opener settings do. Neither names a vault, because the list and the choice belong to the machine. A root that is not a known checkout of the repository is refused (CHECKOUT_UNKNOWN, 404): the page offers nothing else, and the route never registers one. The server watches the registry file from start to stop and follows every change it has not followed yet: the menu's choice, an agent's show or a finished move that chose, a repo command or the first command in a checkout, and another server's show. Then every pane in the vault of a checkout that is not chosen moves to the chosen one, keeping its board, every other pane hears the name its repository goes by now, and every tab hears repositories_changed.

nodes.name: Repository listing
nodes.responsibility: Turns the checkout registry into the repositories the navigator lists: each identity's chosen checkout, its vault and its state, and the names of the vaults
nodes.description: An identity is listed when any known checkout has a vault in the .archboard/vault layout; its state is ready, no-vault, gone or unchosen. The registry is the only source: no environment variable names a vault (TASK-472.09). A vault whose link leads out of the layout is no vault here, because every call to it is refused: its checkout reads no-vault, and an untracked one is not listed. The vault a page opens in is that of the first ready repository by name, else none. repositoryOfVault is how a show names the repository a pane moved into. A vault that no registry entry holds has no repository name, and its checkout is the directory that holds it.

nodes.name: Checkout registry
nodes.responsibility: Which checkouts of each repository this machine knows, which one is chosen, and the untracked vaults

nodes.name: Move route
nodes.responsibility: Moves a whole board into another repository's vault under the write's admission, tells each vault's panes and takes the board's panes along; says beforehand what a move would rewrite
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051: semantic move. move.to names the target vault, read as strictly as the vault of the call. The source vault's change feed says the board moved and where to. A move that stopped part way announces what it wrote, moves no pane, and answers MOVE_STOPPED. TASK-472.16: movePreviewRoute answers GET move-preview, holding and writing nothing, so it takes no lease and no claim; it can be out of date when the move runs, and the version it answers is the version the move states. A board name that cannot be used is refused as every write refuses it (BAD_BOARD_NAME, through usableBoard), and any other refusal is answered in the move's own words and codes.

nodes.name: Board writes
nodes.responsibility: The routes that change a board or its claim: the write boundary, claim, rename, embed tracking, discard and move. Each runs as tracked mutation work, and each change is announced to the panes.

nodes.name: Reads and server health
nodes.responsibility: Routes reads, server health and checkpoint retention without changing current architecture

nodes.name: Code checks on request
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check, locality and footprint when somebody asks, as checkout work, and keeps the last code findings in memory.

nodes.name: Repositories and checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the machine, and knows which checkout holds each repository identity.

nodes.name: Historical correction routes
nodes.responsibility: Prepares a historical correction through the store, reads the code at the revisions it cites with no lease held, and commits exactly the prepared candidate

nodes.name: Track embed route
nodes.responsibility: Lists a tracked embed on a board as a write that needs no stated version, and answers a repeated one with the board unchanged
nodes.description: ADR 0057. semantic render and rasterize --track call it before they write the file.

nodes.name: Canonical model routes
nodes.responsibility: Reads current or exact architecture and retains or lists local checkpoints
nodes.description: Every request names its vault. The shared runtime owns retention, dependency and evidence semantics. Browser selection opens an exact checkpoint through the same read contract.

nodes.name: Local clients
nodes.responsibility: Reads architecture and issues local commands
nodes.description: The browser reader and agent CLI share the local server interface. Each keeps its own role and identity.

nodes.name: Migration planning routes
nodes.responsibility: Translates explicitly addressed inventory and mapping requests into the shared architecture runtime

nodes.name: Archive publication routes
nodes.responsibility: Translates explicit publication and recovery requests without interpreting archive history

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, container interfaces and document references to the code they name, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it

nodes.name: Repository listing

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route carries the claim and the panes to the new name, and keeps what agents said they were doing with the board.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality route keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route asks the store to rename the board. The store carries the claim and what agents said they were doing to the new name, and the route points every pane on the board at the name it has now.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality reading keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none. The history lens reads the board a locality or footprint request names, so the route sends names and maps the refusal to a status.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

beats.heading: A correction reads the code with no lease held
beats.body: A historical correction must be checked against the code at the revisions it cites. The store prepares the candidate first and holds nothing, the route reads Git, and the commit then writes exactly that candidate, refusing it when the board moved while Git was read.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check
nodes.description: The render route reads an optional against: the variant a picture is drawn relative to. It refuses a variant the board lacks, and the drawn variant itself, as an unknown variant.

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write through the store, which moves its claim and what the agent said; points the server's panes at the new name
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, answers its tracked embeds or the nodes that open it, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). A BOARD_OPENED_BY refusal carries openedBy. The pane hears board_note with discarded, reads the board again and finds it missing, as after a move; the browser offers no delete.

nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, the health answer (the archboard-server service, its pid, the checkout whose source it runs and whether that is the source on disk) and the vault a page opens in
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid. A CLI refuses a server whose health names another checkout's source than its own, and names both checkouts. The vault a page opens in is the one call that names no vault.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check, through the one code check the server keeps

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling on request as checkout work: names the board and variant to the history lens, which picks the variant and keeps each answer

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: names the board and proposal to the history lens, which reads them and chooses the variants; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, which needs no vault: the loopback refusal, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant of each vault, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and bound declarations for locality and footprint; reads the board a request names and chooses the variants it reads; labels path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, interfaces and document references to the code they name, at the current variant or the named draft; one run gives behind beside it
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call that names no vault, a vault the server cannot read, or a directory that is not the .archboard/vault of one, before any handler runs
nodes.description: ADR 0049: every call names its vault as ?vault=<directory> or a vault field in its body. The refusal says how to name one (VAULT_REQUIRED, 400; VAULT_UNREADABLE, 404) and creates nothing. TASK-472.09: a vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault is VAULT_UNREADABLE too, and the refusal says to move the boards there, because a workhorse works in the directory that holds the vault (ADR 0050) and such a vault has none. A handler reads the canonical vault with vaultOfRequest.

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which repository identity the vault's own checkout holds, and which checkout holds any other
nodes.description: The board listing needs it: a drill-down that names the vault's own repository is a link within the vault, not a link out of it (ADR 0049).

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it
nodes.description: GET /api/repositories answers under the settings-read browser-origin guard; PUT /api/repositories/chosen {repository, root} answers under the mutation guard, as the opener settings do. Neither names a vault, because the list and the choice belong to the machine. A root that is not a known checkout of the repository is refused (CHECKOUT_UNKNOWN, 404): the page offers nothing else, and the route never registers one. The server watches the registry file from start to stop and follows every change it has not followed yet: the menu's choice, an agent's show or a finished move that chose, a repo command or the first command in a checkout, and another server's show. Then every pane in the vault of a checkout that is not chosen moves to the chosen one, keeping its board, every other pane hears the name its repository goes by now, and every tab hears repositories_changed.

nodes.name: Repository listing
nodes.responsibility: Turns the checkout registry into the repositories the navigator lists: each identity's chosen checkout, its vault and its state, and the names of the vaults
nodes.description: An identity is listed when any known checkout has a vault in the .archboard/vault layout; its state is ready, no-vault, gone or unchosen. The registry is the only source: no environment variable names a vault (TASK-472.09). A vault whose link leads out of the layout is no vault here, because every call to it is refused: its checkout reads no-vault, and an untracked one is not listed. The vault a page opens in is that of the first ready repository by name, else none. repositoryOfVault is how a show names the repository a pane moved into. A vault that no registry entry holds has no repository name, and its checkout is the directory that holds it.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. The file is committed before it answers.

beats.heading: A rename moves more than the board
beats.body: Rename route asks the store to rename the board. The store carries the claim and what agents said they were doing to the new name, and the route points every pane on the board at the name it has now.

beats.heading: A discard tells every pane the board is gone
beats.body: Discard route lets the board go under the write's lease, then tells every pane on it that the board is gone.

beats.heading: A claim keeps the board between writes, and a person can end it
beats.body: Claim routes takes the claim in the board lease and extends it when it is claimed again. A person takes the board back without waiting: the claim ends at once, and the agent hears so once.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality reading keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none. The history lens reads the board a locality or footprint request names, so the route sends names and maps the refusal to a status.

beats.heading: A person chooses a checkout, and every pane reading the old one follows
beats.body: Repository routes accepts only a checkout the registry already knows, makes it the chosen one, moves each pane of the old chosen vault to the new one with its board, and tells every tab to read the repositories again. A board the new checkout has not got is a pane that says so, not a board made on the way.

beats.heading: A move is looked at before it is made
beats.body: The browser asks the move route what moving the board to another repository would rewrite. The store runs the move's own checks against both vaults as they are on disk and writes nothing, so a writer is never kept waiting for a question. The answer carries the board's version, which the move then states.

beats.heading: A correction reads the code with no lease held
beats.body: A historical correction must be checked against the code at the revisions it cites. The store prepares the candidate first and holds nothing, the route reads Git, and the commit then writes exactly that candidate, refusing it when the board moved while Git was read.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check
nodes.description: The render route reads an optional against: the variant a picture is drawn relative to. It refuses a variant the board lacks, and the drawn variant itself, as an unknown variant.

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write through the store, which moves its claim and what the agent said; points the server's panes at the new name
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, answers its tracked embeds or the nodes that open it, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). A BOARD_OPENED_BY refusal carries openedBy. The pane hears board_note with discarded, reads the board again and finds it missing, as after a move; the browser offers no delete.

nodes.name: Service routes
nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, the health answer (the archboard-server service, its pid, the checkout whose source it runs and whether that is the source on disk) and the vault a page opens in
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid. A CLI refuses a server whose health names another checkout's source than its own, and names both checkouts. The vault a page opens in is the one call that names no vault.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check, through the one code check the server keeps

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling on request as checkout work: names the board and variant to the history lens, which picks the variant and keeps each answer

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: names the board and proposal to the history lens, which reads them and chooses the variants; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server, which needs no vault: the loopback refusal, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant of each vault, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and bound declarations for locality and footprint; reads the board a request names and chooses the variants it reads; labels path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships, interfaces and document references to the code they name, at the current variant or the named draft; one run gives behind beside it
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in the vault's own checkout and the chosen ones, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Each document reference of the variant read must name a file at its branch or commit (ADR 0054). Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code.

nodes.name: Vault requirement
nodes.responsibility: Refuses a call that names no vault, a vault the server cannot read, or a directory that is not the .archboard/vault of one, before any handler runs
nodes.description: ADR 0049: every call names its vault as ?vault=<directory> or a vault field in its body. The refusal says how to name one (VAULT_REQUIRED, 400; VAULT_UNREADABLE, 404) and creates nothing. TASK-472.09: a vault whose real path is not <dir>/.archboard/vault is VAULT_UNREADABLE too, and the refusal says to move the boards there, because a workhorse works in the directory that holds the vault (ADR 0050) and such a vault has none. A handler reads the canonical vault with vaultOfRequest.

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which repository identity the vault's own checkout holds, and which checkout holds any other
nodes.description: The board listing needs it: a drill-down that names the vault's own repository is a link within the vault, not a link out of it (ADR 0049).

nodes.name: Repository routes
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the whole machine, and watches the registry file so every pane follows each change, whoever made it
nodes.description: GET /api/repositories answers under the settings-read browser-origin guard; PUT /api/repositories/chosen {repository, root} answers under the mutation guard, as the opener settings do. Neither names a vault, because the list and the choice belong to the machine. A root that is not a known checkout of the repository is refused (CHECKOUT_UNKNOWN, 404): the page offers nothing else, and the route never registers one. The server watches the registry file from start to stop and follows every change it has not followed yet: the menu's choice, an agent's show or a finished move that chose, a repo command or the first command in a checkout, and another server's show. Then every pane in the vault of a checkout that is not chosen moves to the chosen one, keeping its board, every other pane hears the name its repository goes by now, and every tab hears repositories_changed.

nodes.name: Repository listing
nodes.responsibility: Turns the checkout registry into the repositories the navigator lists: each identity's chosen checkout, its vault and its state, and the names of the vaults
nodes.description: An identity is listed when any known checkout has a vault in the .archboard/vault layout; its state is ready, no-vault, gone or unchosen. The registry is the only source: no environment variable names a vault (TASK-472.09). A vault whose link leads out of the layout is no vault here, because every call to it is refused: its checkout reads no-vault, and an untracked one is not listed. The vault a page opens in is that of the first ready repository by name, else none. repositoryOfVault is how a show names the repository a pane moved into. A vault that no registry entry holds has no repository name, and its checkout is the directory that holds it.

nodes.name: Checkout registry
nodes.responsibility: Which checkouts of each repository this machine knows, which one is chosen, and the untracked vaults

nodes.name: Move route
nodes.responsibility: Moves a whole board into another repository's vault under the write's admission, tells each vault's panes and takes the board's panes along; says beforehand what a move would rewrite
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051: semantic move. move.to names the target vault, read as strictly as the vault of the call. The source vault's change feed says the board moved and where to. A move that stopped part way announces what it wrote, moves no pane, and answers MOVE_STOPPED. TASK-472.16: movePreviewRoute answers GET move-preview, holding and writing nothing, so it takes no lease and no claim; it can be out of date when the move runs, and the version it answers is the version the move states. A board name that cannot be used is refused as every write refuses it (BAD_BOARD_NAME, through usableBoard), and any other refusal is answered in the move's own words and codes.

nodes.name: Architecture writes
nodes.responsibility: Applies architecture changes and tracks accepted writes through shutdown

nodes.name: Reads and server health
nodes.responsibility: Routes reads, server health and checkpoint retention without changing current architecture

nodes.name: Code checks on request
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check, locality and footprint when somebody asks, as checkout work, and keeps the last code findings in memory.

nodes.name: Repositories and checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Lists the repositories the navigator shows, chooses a repository's checkout for the machine, and knows which checkout holds each repository identity.

nodes.name: Historical correction routes
nodes.responsibility: Prepares a historical correction through the store, reads the code at the revisions it cites with no lease held, and commits exactly the prepared candidate

nodes.name: Track embed route
nodes.responsibility: Lists a tracked embed on a board as a write that needs no stated version, and answers a repeated one with the board unchanged
nodes.description: ADR 0057. semantic render and rasterize --track call it before they write the file.

nodes.name: Canonical model routes
nodes.responsibility: Reads current or exact architecture and retains or lists local checkpoints
nodes.description: Every request names its vault. The shared runtime owns retention, dependency and evidence semantics. Browser selection opens an exact checkpoint through the same read contract. Canonical edit, claim and recovery adapters use the shared operation contract. A vault-scoped event stream sends fresh coherent readings and durable news.

nodes.name: Local clients
nodes.responsibility: Reads architecture and issues local commands
nodes.description: The browser reader and agent CLI share the local server interface. Each keeps its own role and identity.

nodes.name: Migration planning routes
nodes.responsibility: Translates explicitly addressed inventory and mapping requests into the shared architecture runtime

nodes.name: Canonical edit routes
nodes.responsibility: Adapts description edits, claims, recovery and fresh current event streams
nodes.description: Every call names a vault. Mutation work stays tracked through response loss and shutdown. Shared runtime contracts own claims, durable completion and recovery. The browser presentation remains parent-owned TASK-549.03 work.

nodes.name: Mutation work
nodes.responsibility: Tracks accepted mutation work through response loss and server shutdown

nodes.name: Archive publication routes
nodes.responsibility: Translates explicit publication and recovery requests without interpreting archive history
